content.text:
I have the evidence I need. Incumbent truth (critique 2026-09-15T19-30, 25/40, H1 = 2) plus code reading: - **Row pill** `StatePills` (`components/queue/row-cells.tsx:32`) derives its word from its own props (`approved={bill.status === "reviewed"}`, `inReview={approvalStatus === "in_progress"}`), *not* from `processingState()` — so it can disagree with the leading glyph (#223) on the same row, and has a sixth word, **Unreviewed**, that is not in CONTEXT.md's list. - **Pane pill** (`split-pane.tsx:236`) prints the raw `Document.status` string with underscores swapped — **reviewed / needs review / ready for review / queued / failed**: the persistence vocabulary, not the operator's. - **Stepper** (`documents/[documentId]/page.tsx:211`) says **Approval — signed off / in review / awaiting approval**. - **Approval tab** (`history-tabs.tsx:25`) says **"No approval steps yet. Approving this document records the first one."** even when the row says Approved. - The audit log already holds `document_reviewed` (label "Document reviewed") with actor + timestamp, and `review_task_stage_decided` for flow stages — the who/when exists. - Facet options add **Unreviewed · Reviewed · Synced** (Invoices "Open" group) and `STAGE_LABELS` adds **Inbox · Review**. Vic (§6, tour §1) keeps two axes: *Status* (Unreviewed/Reviewed → Posted/Exported) and *Invoice Approval* (Not Started/In Progress/Approved/Rejected/Cancelled), and its Approval tab is STEP n → decision, named user, reason, INITIATED footer. Mode: **Operate**. Surface is being *refined* (the pane stays), so the 25/40 critique is the evidence baseline. ## Round 1 — the vocabulary itself (Intent: `articulate`) ❓ **Q1** - **One word list**: CONTEXT.md's Processing state is five words: Cancelled · Needs attention · In review · Touchless · Approved. The row pill adds *Unreviewed*, the pane adds the raw status strings, the stepper adds *signed off*, the facets add *Unreviewed/Reviewed*, the legacy pipeline adds *Inbox/Review*. Is the Processing-state list the single vocabulary for everything that says where a document stands, with no sixth word? ➡️ Yes — exactly the five, everywhere a processing state is spoken. *Unreviewed* is not a state: a document nobody has opened is **In review** (processingState already treats `status !== "reviewed"` as in_review, #223's resolution). *Reviewed* is the persistence value, never shown. *Signed off* is a synonym and Vic's §6 table never uses it. Evidence: critique H1=2 and H4=2 both trace to synonyms; Intent Category 9 *Inconsistent Patterns*; `clarify`: "Keep the same noun and verb for the same concept throughout the product." --- ❓ **Q2** - **One derivation, not four**: today each surface computes its own word from different inputs (row pill from `status`/`approvalStatus`; pane pill from `Document.status`; stepper from `openReviewTask`+`status`). Do all four read from the one `processingState()` function, with `BillRow`-shaped input threaded to the pane and stepper? ➡️ Yes. A vocabulary that is shared but derived four ways still disagrees (the pill and the glyph on the same row already can: escalated → glyph *Needs attention*, pill *Approved*). `processingState()` is the one source; the pane receives the row's `ProcessingStateInput` (or the computed state) alongside the document. Evidence: Intent principle *Make intent visible* / feedback loops; craft rule "one place the app spells the lifecycle out" (`stages.ts` comment already asks for it). --- ❓ **Q3** - **Ledger facts stay a second axis**: CONTEXT.md says Synced/Paid are not processing states. Does the pane keep showing them, and as what? ➡️ Yes, as the same second pill `StatePills` already renders after the state (`ledger` prop), lower-case-free: **Synced** · **Paid** · **Reconciled**; never merged into the state word. Vic (tour §1) keeps *Status* and *Invoice Approval* as separate facets; #229 derives Paid ledger-first (ADR 0001). No change to the axis, only to where it renders (Q5). --- ❓ **Q4** - **Facet and legacy labels follow**: the Invoices facet "Open: Unreviewed · Reviewed · Synced" and Receipts "Unreviewed · Reviewed" use the old words. Do they switch to the five states + ledger facts? ➡️ Yes: the Status facet becomes **Processing state** (Cancelled · Needs attention · In review · Touchless · Approved) and **Ledger** (Synced · Paid), matching Vic's two-facet hierarchy (§6: hierarchical sub-toggles under one chip). `STAGE_LABELS` (`Inbox/Review/Approved/Synced/Paid`) survives only for the public API's `stage` aliases and the retired pipeline page — it is not shown on the queue. Evidence: the "Not yet specified" fog on facet parity; critique H4. ## Round 1 answers (owner's delegation — recommendations taken) Q1 ➡️ five words, no sixth. Q2 ➡️ one `processingState()` source. Q3 ➡️ ledger stays a second pill. Q4 ➡️ facets rename; `STAGE_LABELS` stays API-only. Rule: map Notes (#177 baseline: CONTEXT.md Processing state, #222/#223) + `clarify` reference. ## Round 2 — which elements survive, and the Approval tab (Intent: `fortify`; Impeccable: `clarify`) ❓ **Q5** - **Does the pane pill survive?** With the row pill visible in the narrowed list at 1440 (the critique notes the State column *drops* when the pane opens) and the stepper's Approval node also carrying the state, the pane says it three times. Options: (a) keep pane pill as `StatePills`, (b) drop it and let the stepper carry it, (c) drop it and put a one-line status sentence in the pane header. ➡️ **(c)**: the pane pill as an element is retired; the pane header carries **one status line** — the state word rendered as the same `StatePills` (same component, same colours, plus the ledger pill), followed by the fact behind it: *"Approved by Nadia K. · 12 Sep 2026"*, *"In review · opened 3 days ago"*, *"Needs attention · 2 open checks"*, *"Touchless · sent automatically, all fields ≥ 90%"*, *"Cancelled · duplicate of INV-118"*. This mirrors Vic's batch-detail sheet summary strip (§6: submitted by, bills, total, bank — facts, not a pill). The State column returns to the narrowed list only if #235 decides so; the pane's status line is what the operator reads while the pane is open. Layout position of the line inside the header stack is #234's call (this ticket blocks it). Evidence: critique H8=2 "document introduces itself four times"; `clarify` "say each idea once". --- ❓ **Q6** - **Does the stepper survive, and what does its Approval node say?** Extracted → Checks → Approval → Sync → Pay is a DocuBite-only element (Vic has none). Its node details today are *signed off / in review / awaiting approval / all clear / pushed × n / confirmed paid*. ➡️ Survives (that is #234's structural call; the Notes' documented exception keeps the combined pane) — but its node *details* speak the same vocabulary: Approval node detail = the state word (**Approved**, **In review**, **Needs attention**, **Touchless**, **Cancelled**) — never *signed off*; Sync/Pay node details are the ledger facts (**Synced × n**, **Push failed**, **Paid**, **Paid in ledger**); Checks detail = **All clear** or the first blocker. Nothing on the stepper may say a word the pill doesn't. Evidence: Q1; critique H1. --- ❓ **Q7** - **Approval tab for a document approved without stage decisions** (workflow-less review; today "No approval steps yet"). What does it say, from where? ➡️ It is never empty on an Approved document. Three cases, all from the audit log (`review_task_stage_decided` for flow stages, `document_reviewed` for the workflow-less sign-off, extraction/autopublish events for Touchless): - **Approved without a flow**: one step row, same shape as a stage row — *"Reviewed and approved by ‹actor› · ‹date time›"* with a footer *"No approval flow ran — approved from the queue."* (Vic's INITIATED footer analogue, §6.) - **Touchless**: *"Sent automatically · ‹date time› — all fields met the 90% threshold; nobody reviewed it."* (CONTEXT.md: Touchless is shown as a fact once it has happened.) - **In review, no flow started**: the empty state names the next action honestly: *"No approval started. Start approval from the Invoices bulk bar, or approve from the pane."* — not "Approving this document records the first one" (which promised a step that a workflow-less approve doesn't write to the step chain). - **Needs attention / rejected**: the rejecting step with its reason stays the top row (already built, #218). - **Cancelled**: *"Approval cancelled by ‹actor› · ‹date› — ‹reason›"*. Evidence: tour §1 "a real audit trail with human accountability… not just a status enum"; CONTEXT.md Approval; Intent *Evidence*/*visible intent*; `clarify` "do not promise a resolution the system cannot know". --- ❓ **Q8** - **Naming the tab**: should the tab stay "Approval" when it now also explains Touchless and a workflow-less sign-off? ➡️ Stays **Approval**. The tab answers "who decided this and when" in every case; renaming it (e.g. "Decision") would break #227/#232's settled tab set (Approval · Details · Checks · History). Rule: smallest reversible option; #232 named the tabs. ## Round 2 answers Q5 ➡️ (c) status line = `StatePills` + fact sentence; pane pill element retired. Q6 ➡️ stepper survives, node details use the five words + ledger facts. Q7 ➡️ Approval tab reads from the audit log, five cases. Q8 ➡️ tab keeps its name. ## Round 3 — states, copy matrix, accessibility (fortify · include · clarify) ❓ **Q9** - **Fact-sentence source when the audit row is missing**: an old document approved before `document_reviewed` was logged, or an actor deleted (actor SetNull). What renders? ➡️ Degrade honestly: *"Approved · ‹reviewedAt date›"* when the event has no actor (`Document.reviewedAt` is always set on approve); *"Approved"* alone only if both are absent. Never invent a name; never say "by System" for a human approval (the audit log already renders "System" only for actor-less events). Evidence: `fortify` partial state; `clarify` "do not promise a cause the system cannot know". --- ❓ **Q10** - **Accessible name and announcement**: the status line's `StatePills` are colour + text; the row's glyph (#223) already has an accessible name = the state word. ➡️ The status line is a `

` with the state word first in DOM order, so a screen reader hears "Approved by Nadia K., 12 September 2026" once; the pill's colour is not the only channel (text is). On a decision the line updates via the existing `aria-live` region the pane already uses for `1 of 4`. No extra role. Evidence: `include` — WCAG 1.4.1 use of colour; critique Sam persona. --- ❓ **Q11** - **Capitalisation and tense**: *Needs attention* (present), *Approved* (past), *In review* (state), *Touchless* (adjective). ➡️ Keep CONTEXT.md's exact forms, sentence case, as-is; the mixed grammatical form is fine because each is the operator's own phrase (Vic's list — Not Started / In Progress / Approved / Rejected — mixes tenses the same way). The only rule: identical string everywhere, from one constant map `PROCESSING_STATE_LABELS`. Evidence: `clarify` "inconsistent terminology and capitalization" is the defect, not tense. --- ❓ **Q12** - **Receipts and the other queues**: same words? ➡️ Yes, unchanged — `processingState()` already runs on `ReceiptRow` (#223); Bank Statements/POs/Exceptions rows that have no approval carry only In review / Approved / Needs attention. Bank statements' stepper stops at Sync (already built). ## Round 3 answers Q9 ➡️ degrade to date, then word alone. Q10 ➡️ text-first `

`, existing live region. Q11 ➡️ exact CONTEXT.md strings from one label map. Q12 ➡️ all queues. Frontier is empty. Recording the decision: glossary first, then the resolution.

content.content:
118	**Queue screen**:
119	A typed destination's list view (Invoices, Purchase Orders, Receipts, Bank Statements, Exceptions). The queue fills the work area; selecting a row opens the Detail pane beside it, and the operator never leaves the screen to review, approve, or resolve a row.
120	
121	**Detail pane**:
122	The single right-hand pane on a Queue screen that shows the selected row's extracted fields beside its source document, with its approval chain, audit trail, and open checks as tabs. There is one Detail pane per Queue screen; it is the only place a row's detail opens in place. On a phone the same pane opens full-screen over the queue, with the source document stacked above the fields and the decision bar at the bottom; it is still the Detail pane, not a second screen.
123	_Avoid_: Approval Context (Vic's separate phone screen — DocuBite has one pane), detail sheet
124	
125	**Origin context**:
126	The workspace, list, filters, position, and workflow state from which a user opened a detail or action surface. Returning from that surface restores the origin context whenever it still exists.
127	
128	**Workflow operation**:
129	An in-progress or recently completed unit of work such as extraction, sync, review assignment, worksheet placement, approval, or publish. An operation remains discoverable after navigation so the user can understand what happened and what to do next.
130	
131	**Operation status**:
132	The user-facing progress and outcome for a workflow operation, shown inline where the operation began and in the workspace activity/status area. It includes the current step, progress when known, and a plain-language next action.
133	
134	**Partial outcome**:
135	A batch result in which individual items may succeed, need review, be skipped, be canceled, or fail. Partial outcomes remain visible per item rather than being collapsed into one batch-level success or failure.
136	
137	**Server-confirmed action**:
138	An action whose durable or external effect is not treated as complete until the server confirms it, including approvals, ledger pushes, and other financial writes. Local optimistic feedback may precede confirmation only for reversible, low-risk changes.
139	
140	**Touchless**:
141	A document whose extracted fields all met the workspace's confidence threshold and was pushed to the ledger without a human review step. Shown on a record as a fact once it has happened, not as a prediction or a pending state.
142	_Avoid_: Auto-approved, zero-touch
143	
144	**Processing state**:
145	Where a queue row stands in the intake → review → approval path, shown as one mark at the row's leading edge. Exactly one of, in precedence order: Cancelled, Needs attention (a check blocked it, an escalation is open, or an approval was rejected), In review, Touchless, Approved. **Queue screen**:
A typed destination's list view (Invoices, Purchase Orders, Receipts, Bank Statements, Exceptions). The queue fills the work area; selecting a row opens the Detail pane beside it, and the operator never leaves the screen to review, approve, or resolve a row.

**Detail pane**:
The single right-hand pane on a Queue screen that shows the selected row's extracted fields beside its source document, with its approval chain, audit trail, and open checks as tabs. There is one Detail pane per Queue screen; it is the only place a row's detail opens in place. On a phone the same pane opens full-screen over the queue, with the source document stacked above the fields and the decision bar at the bottom; it is still the Detail pane, not a second screen.
_Avoid_: Approval Context (Vic's separate phone screen — DocuBite has one pane), detail sheet

**Origin context**:
The workspace, list, filters, position, and workflow state from which a user opened a detail or action surface. Returning from that surface restores the origin context whenever it still exists.

**Workflow operation**:
An in-progress or recently completed unit of work such as extraction, sync, review assignment, worksheet placement, approval, or publish. An operation remains discoverable after navigation so the user can understand what happened and what to do next.

**Operation status**:
The user-facing progress and outcome for a workflow operation, shown inline where the operation began and in the workspace activity/status area. It includes the current step, progress when known, and a plain-language next action.

**Partial outcome**:
A batch result in which individual items may succeed, need review, be skipped, be canceled, or fail. Partial outcomes remain visible per item rather than being collapsed into one batch-level success or failure.

**Server-confirmed action**:
An action whose durable or external effect is not treated as complete until the server confirms it, including approvals, ledger pushes, and other financial writes. Local optimistic feedback may precede confirmation only for reversible, low-risk changes.

**Touchless**:
A document whose extracted fields all met the workspace's confidence threshold and was pushed to the ledger without a human review step. Shown on a record as a fact once it has happened, not as a prediction or a pending state.
_Avoid_: Auto-approved, zero-touch

**Processing state**:
Where a queue row stands in the intake → review → approval path, shown as one mark at the row's leading edge. Exactly one of, in precedence order: Cancelled, Needs attention (a check blocked it, an escalation is open, or an approval was rejected), In review, Touchless, Approved. Ledger facts such as Synced or Paid are not processing states and are shown separately. Due-date urgency is not a processing state either.
_Avoid_: Status (the column of pills is broader), aging (that is the due-date signal)

**Confidence threshold**:
The single workspace-set score an extracted field must reach to count as confident. It is the same floor Touchless is judged against, so a field that clears it in a queue row would also clear it for Touchless. A field entered by a person, or never scored by extraction, has no confidence and shows no confidence claim at all — absence means "not an AI claim", not "low".

# TaxHacker Product Context

This glossary defines the product language used for the authenticated workspace experience and its document-to-ledger workflow.

## Authenticated workspace experience

**Workspace home**:
The Invoices queue. Opening a workspace lands the user on their work, not on a summary of it; "what needs me" is read from the rail badges and the queue's own counts. There is no separate overview surface.
_Avoid_: Dashboard, landing page, overview, next best action

**Unplugged surface**:
A feature the product no longer shows or routes to, kept only so it can be brought back deliberately. Worksheets, Expenses and Dictation are unplugged. An unplugged surface has no navigation entry, no row or bulk action, no badge, and its addresses do not open.
_Avoid_: Hidden, deprecated, legacy

**Core workflow destinations**:
Invoices, Purchase Orders, Receipts, Bank Statements, Exceptions, Finance, and Archive: the permission-filtered peer surfaces representing typed intake, escalated work, booked outcome, and the permanent source record. The four typed intake destinations replace the former single "Documents" surface.

**Document**:
The storage-and-extraction primitive underlying every typed destination. Every Invoice, Purchase Order, Receipt, and Bank Statement is a Document, but "Document" is no longer itself a user-facing destination — the user asserts which typed destination a Document belongs to at upload time, and that assertion is authoritative.
_Avoid_: Using "Document" as a destination name; unclassified/pending-classification states

**Invoice**:
The typed destination for a bill received from a supplier. Absorbs the former Documents/Bills surface; aging is a filter chip and a saved view here, and paying an approved invoice happens on Bill Pay, not on this queue.

**Purchase Order**:
The typed destination for a purchase order, paired with Invoices for matching and cumulative line-item comparison against what has already been invoiced against it.

**Receipt**:
The typed destination for a receipt. Absorbs expense-claim creation and approval as an action on selected rows rather than as its own destination.

**Bank Statement**:
The typed destination for a bank statement. The reviewer asserts the issuing institution; the first statement for that institution becomes its saved layout, and later uploads are checked against it for drift.

**Check**:
A tri-valued (pass/warn/fail), explainable comparison that states in plain language why a value is flagged, anchored to the field, cell, or row it concerns. "Mismatch" names one Check status, not the category.
_Avoid_: Discrepancy, issue, error (as the umbrella term)

**Line match**:
An invoice line's assigned Purchase Order line — guessed by description similarity, or set by hand in Match manually. A line below the similarity threshold has no line match and is not compared.
_Avoid_: Line pairing, line mapping

**Match manually**:
The named in-row mode on an invoice's line items that confirms, replaces or rejects its Purchase Order and reassigns line matches; the checks re-run when it is left. It changes the facts and needs no reason; it is not Override Mode, which accepts a variance with a reason.
_Avoid_: Manual Match Mode (Vic's name), re-match, Override (for a match change)

**Override Mode**:
The screen-scoped mode in which a soft check or gate can be overridden, each override attributed and recorded with a required reason. Hard gates are out of its reach.
_Avoid_: Bypass, force approve

**Fully invoiced**:
A Purchase Order whose every line has been invoiced to at least its ordered quantity. Derived, never set by hand.
_Avoid_: Closed PO, consumed

**Saved view**:
A named, reusable filter/sort/column configuration on a list screen. System views are seeded per screen and are not editable or deletable; a user can duplicate one into an editable, optionally shared, view.

**Work item**:
A single unit of pending work surfaced in a Next-action queue — a document awaiting review or a match awaiting confirmation. An approval awaiting a decision is an Approval, not a work item; it is worked by an Approver, not an assignee.

**Approval**:
A run started on an invoice by a person, moving through the stages of an approval flow until it is approved, rejected, or sent back for review. An invoice nobody has started an approval on is under review, not awaiting approval.
_Avoid_: Review task (the storage record), sign-off (as the umbrella term)

**Approver**:
The person who can decide the current stage of an Approval — a stage's named approver, or any owner where the stage names nobody. Distinct from an assignee, who works a review.
_Avoid_: Reviewer (that is who prepares the row), assignee

**Ready to Approve**:
The personal system view on the Approvals destination: every Approval whose current stage the signed-in person can decide, including rows that are not yet eligible, shown with the reason. The badge on the rail counts this view and nothing else.
_Avoid_: Pending approvals (that is the workspace-wide count), inbox

**Send back for review**:
The reversible middle path on an Approval: the stage is not decided, the invoice returns to review with a required reason, and the run can be restarted. Reject ends the run.
_Avoid_: Reopen, cancel (that withdraws a run before any stage is decided)

**Not eligible**:
An Approval that is visible to its Approver but cannot be decided yet because a hard check failed or an escalation is open on the invoice. Never hidden, never overridable from Approvals; the reason is shown on the row.

**Bill Pay**:
The queue of approved, unpaid invoices from which payment batches are created. An invoice reaches it only once its processing state is Approved; one that cannot be paid yet (no supplier bank details) stays visible with the reason.
_Avoid_: Payables, payment run (the queue), pay list

**Payment batch**:
A named set of approved invoices, one payer account and one currency, submitted by a member for an owner's decision. Pending approval, then Approved (its payment file can be downloaded), then Paid; or Rejected with a reason. Whether the file has been downloaded is a fact shown on the batch, not a state. A batch never moves money.
_Avoid_: Payment run, remittance (that is the advice sent to the supplier), transfer

**Payer account**:
A named workspace bank account a payment batch is to be paid from — a label that tells the uploader which bank portal the file belongs to. DocuBite never holds the account's credentials and the file never carries its number.
_Avoid_: Pay From (Vic's column label is fine on screen; the concept is the payer account), funding source, bank connection

**Payment terms**:
A supplier's net days and, when offered, an early-payment discount: the percent and the days within which it applies, shown as "2/10 net 30". A supplier without a discount shows no discount claim and no discount countdown.
_Avoid_: Terms code, "2-10-30"

**Payment record**:
A DocuBite-side fact that an amount was paid against an invoice on a date, by a batch or by hand (Mark as paid). An invoice's paid state is derived from the ledger when it confirms payment, otherwise from its payment records. A payment record can be removed with a reason.
_Avoid_: Mark as paid (the action, not the record), settlement, ledger payment (that is the ledger's own line)

**Company**:
The user-facing name for a team workspace in Admin and the switcher: one legal or financial entity with its own currency, tax jurisdiction, suppliers, ledger and members. "Workspace" remains the storage and address term. The auto-created personal workspace is shown as Personal, never as a company.
_Avoid_: Entity (Vic's word), tenant, client (that is who the company belongs to)

**Organization**:
A named group of companies an accountant or finance team runs under one login. Belonging to an organization never by itself opens any of its companies; access to each company is granted separately, with its own role.
_Avoid_: Firm (the derived workspace mode), account, tenant

**Admin**:
The desktop-only area, reached from the bottom of the rail, that holds every setting: Organization (Dashboard, Companies, Users) and the current Company (Configuration, Approval Flows, PO Mismatch Flows, Suppliers, Integrations). Account-level settings (security, sign out) live in the account menu, not in Admin. Admin › Dashboard is the per-company triage rollup for an organization with more than one company; it is not the workspace home.
_Avoid_: Settings (as the area's name), Controls (folded into Configuration), preferences

**Configuration**:
The Admin section that says what a company's queues and Detail pane show and what may happen without a person: the per-type field table (Editable, Required, Width), the autonomy level and what blocks a publish, tax, email intake and what is switched on. Every switch carries one sentence saying what it changes.
_Avoid_: Automation settings, workspace settings

**Immersive surface**:
A document-detail or worksheet page that temporarily takes over the viewport while preserving workspace identity, a clear return action, and relevant workspace status.

**Queue screen**:
A typed destination's list view (Invoices, Purchase Orders, Receipts, Bank Statements, Exceptions). The queue fills the work area; selecting a row opens the Detail pane beside it, and the operator never leaves the screen to review, approve, or resolve a row.

**Detail pane**:
The single right-hand pane on a Queue screen that shows the selected row's extracted fields beside its source document, with its approval chain, audit trail, and open checks as tabs. There is one Detail pane per Queue screen; it is the only place a row's detail opens in place. On a phone the same pane opens full-screen over the queue, with the source document stacked above the fields and the decision bar at the bottom; it is still the Detail pane, not a second screen.
_Avoid_: Approval Context (Vic's separate phone screen — DocuBite has one pane), detail sheet

**Origin context**:
The workspace, list, filters, position, and workflow state from which a user opened a detail or action surface. Returning from that surface restores the origin context whenever it still exists.

**Workflow operation**:
An in-progress or recently completed unit of work such as extraction, sync, review assignment, worksheet placement, approval, or publish. An operation remains discoverable after navigation so the user can understand what happened and what to do next.

**Operation status**:
The user-facing progress and outcome for a workflow operation, shown inline where the operation began and in the workspace activity/status area. It includes the current step, progress when known, and a plain-language next action.

**Partial outcome**:
A batch result in which individual items may succeed, need review, be skipped, be canceled, or fail. Partial outcomes remain visible per item rather than being collapsed into one batch-level success or failure.

**Server-confirmed action**:
An action whose durable or external effect is not treated as complete until the server confirms it, including approvals, ledger pushes, and other financial writes. Local optimistic feedback may precede confirmation only for reversible, low-risk changes.

**Touchless**:
A document whose extracted fields all met the workspace's confidence threshold and was pushed to the ledger without a human review step. Shown on a record as a fact once it has happened, not as a prediction or a pending state.
_Avoid_: Auto-approved, zero-touch

**Processing state**:
Where a queue row stands in the intake → review → approval path, shown as one mark at the row's leading edge. Exactly one of, in precedence order: Cancelled, Needs attention (a check blocked it, an escalation is open, or an approval was rejected), In review, Touchless, Approved. Ledger facts such as Synced or Paid are not processing states and are shown separately. Due-date urgency is not a processing state either.
_Avoid_: Status (the column of pills is broader), aging (that is the due-date signal)

**Confidence threshold**:
The single workspace-set score an extracted field must reach to count as confident. It is the same floor Touchless is judged against, so a field that clears it in a queue row would also clear it for Touchless. A field entered by a person, or never scored by extraction, has no confidence and shows no confidence claim at all — absence means "not an AI claim", not "low".
_Avoid_: High confidence, low confidence (as if they were fixed numbers), the internal stage cutoff or amount-band floors (those are gates, not the user-facing threshold)

## Public marketing and coverage

**Supported coverage**:
A jurisdiction with a registered, working jurisdiction pack that can support the relevant document-to-ledger workflow.
_Avoid_: Global support, available everywhere

**Roadmap coverage**:
A jurisdiction the product may support later but cannot currently accept for the relevant workflow. It must not be presented as available or used to qualify a current signup promise.
_Avoid_: Supported, coming soon (unless the rollout is an explicit product commitment)

**Trial**:
A time-bounded product-access period with an explicit start, expiry, and billing or cancellation path. DocuBite must not use this term publicly until those supporting paths exist.
_Avoid_: Free workspace, evaluation

**Account creation**:
The current public entry action: creating a DocuBite account before setting up or joining a workspace. It is not a trial start or a payment event.
_Avoid_: Start free trial, Subscribe

**Workspace storage cap**:
The hard limit of 200 MB of stored documents per workspace. It must be disclosed before an upload is accepted, even when it is omitted from the marketing CTA.
_Avoid_: Unlimited storage

**Connected accounting system**:
An external accounting platform a workspace can connect to today, currently QuickBooks Online or Xero.
_Avoid_: Available integration when the connector is not live

**Built-in ledger**:
DocuBite's own double-entry ledger destination. It is a product capability, not an external integration.
_Avoid_: Third-party integration

**Planned integration**:
A named future accounting destination shown as roadmap intent, not as a capability available today. Planned integrations must not be presented with vendor marks without approved permission.
_Avoid_: Supported, connected, coming soon

**Product capability**:
A public-facing product area organized around one coherent mechanism and the visitor outcome it enables. The current capability vocabulary is Document extraction, Controls & fraud, Close the books, Data health, and Integrations & API.
_Avoid_: Feature list, module

**Product overview**:
The public entry point that orients visitors to the product capability set before directing them to detailed capability pages.
_Avoid_: Feature dump, single-scroll feature wall

**Trust & security**:
The procurement-facing explanation of DocuBite's safeguards, data handling, access controls, auditability, and compliance posture. It is a trust destination, not a Product capability.
_Avoid_: Security feature, compliance promise

**Solution**:
A role-oriented explanation of how DocuBite fits a team's workflow. Document types describe capabilities and belong with Product, not with the role-oriented Solutions structure.
_Avoid_: Document type, industry page

**Document extraction**:
The Product capability that turns supported PDFs and images into reviewable structured rows with visible confidence and source provenance. It describes the extraction and review mechanism, not a guarantee that every input is readable.
_Avoid_: Perfect OCR, quality rescue

**Controls & fraud**:
The Product capability that applies explainable checks, gates, approval rules, and human review before risky workflow steps.
_Avoid_: Fraud prevention guarantee, autonomous approval

**Close the books**:
The Product capability that coordinates close checklists, gated period transitions, accrual drafts, aging, matching, and related month-end work.
_Avoid_: Automatic close, payment execution

**Data health**:
The Product capability that surfaces scored pipeline, ledger, and tax hygiene so teams can find drift before it becomes a reconciliation problem.
_Avoid_: Data correctness guarantee, audit certification

**Integrations & API**:
The Product capability for sending reviewed data to the built-in ledger, connected accounting systems, and workspace-scoped external systems through documented API and webhook surfaces.
_Avoid_: Universal integration, available connector when it is only planned

**Capability page**:
A detailed public Product page organized around one outcome, one mechanism, evidence-backed proof points, explicit limits, and one account-creation action.
_Avoid_: Feature dump, unsupported promise

`; announced through the pane's existing live region on a decision. ## Destination

DocuBite's authenticated app works the way Vic.ai's does, end to end: **Vic's interaction grammar, DocuBite's skin.** Every operator surface — Invoices, Purchase Orders, Receipts, Bank Statements, Exceptions, Approvals (Invoices / PO Mismatches), Bill Pay, Payment Batches, and Admin — shares one shell: a full-width 62px queue, one header band (View · Sort · summary filter chips opening a hierarchical facet panel), a bulk action row, and one right-hand Detail pane with a sticky bottom action bar. PO mismatches are resolved on the invoice row with per-cell match glyphs and the tolerance arithmetic in view. Payment runs are batched, approved and exported without DocuBite moving money. Admin is a distinct area (Configuration, Approval Flows, Mismatch Flows, Users, Companies) with multi-company access. Approval works on a phone. Implemented and shipped, measured by Impeccable's in-page detector and a critique score above the 20/40 baseline on every queue.

Evidence: the full self-guided tour walked 2026-09-15 — `docs/vic-ai-ux-tour-findings.md` §6 and the screenshots in `docs/vic-ai-tour-2026-09-15/` (DocuBite's own Invoices screen from the same day sits beside them).

## Notes

**Supersedes [Map: Vic.ai-style typed AP surfaces (#177)](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/177).** #177's thirty closed decisions are this map's baseline and are cited, not re-decided. Its two open tickets, [Build the five-state processing glyph (#223)](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/223) and [Build the typed list-screen composition on all five queues (#225)](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/225), are re-parented here. #177 is closed.

**Why a second map.** #177 reached its destination as feature slices bolted onto the old pages, with no ticket owning composition and no in-browser verification, and scored 20/40 ([#224](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/224)). This map charts by *surface*, each ticket owning a whole screen's shape, and every execution ticket closes on detector counts.

**Execution mode.** This map carries execution. Decision tickets resolve first; each spawns an execution ticket; execution tickets close only with `impeccable` run at the four points in CLAUDE.md, in-page detector before/after counts at 1440 and 390 (list and pane-open), and `polish`. Dev-server + seed + headless-Chromium recipe is on #225.

**Design protocol.** Every rendered-surface ticket calls the Skill tool for `impeccable` (sub-command named on the ticket) and `intent`, before the work. Grilling tickets on a surface open with `impeccable critique` of the incumbent and cite the tour screenshot they are matching.

**Vic wins ties, with the tour as the record.** "Does this follow Vic or DocuBite?" defaults to Vic without asking, and the answer is read off `docs/vic-ai-ux-tour-findings.md` §6 and the screenshots — not from memory of the older sections. Grill only what the tour does not settle: DocuBite-only features (Exceptions, Touchless, does-not-move-money, bank statements, institutions), data DocuBite lacks (payment terms, discounts, buyers, entities), and anything that would reverse a #177 decision.

**Documented exceptions to Vic** (decided, do not re-open by "Vic wins ties"): the combined fields+source Detail pane (#179 → #224) with History as its tabs instead of Vic's left panel; the collapsible icon rail instead of Vic's top bar (#224 Q5); DocuBite's palette, type and emerald brand (this map, Q2); Exceptions as its own destination (#192); Touchless keeps its name.

**Settled while charting (grilled 2026-09-15):**

- **Scope is the whole operator app** — queues + Detail pane, Approvals inbox, PO matching in the row, Bill Pay + Payment Batches, Admin, mobile approval. One grammar everywhere.
- **Fidelity is grammar, not skin.** Same layouts, panels, chips, bars, keyboard flow, copy patterns; colour and type stay DocuBite's.
- **Payments never move money.** Bill Pay queue (open bills, terms, countdown, discounted amount over struck-through due) and Payment Batches queue (batch → approve → export file). The transfer stays outside DocuBite, as `preparePaymentRun` does today.
- **Approvals is a destination with two queues**, Invoices and PO Mismatches, each a personal Ready-to-Approve view with the sticky Approve/Reject bar. Exceptions stays separate.
- **Admin adopts Vic's full IA including Companies**: Configuration (per-field Editable/Required/Width, consequence toggles), Approval Flows, PO Mismatch Flows, Users, Companies — one login, many companies, per-entity permissions. This is the one schema-and-auth effort on the map; it is researched before it is grilled.
- **Build order:** shell (#225) → distill (#238) → Approvals → PO matching → Payments → Admin → Mobile.
- **Removal protocol (owner's rule, #237):** nothing is removed from the app without the owner signing off each removal by name on the ticket. Removed features are *unplugged* (CONTEXT.md term), not deleted, so a return is a re-link.

## Decisions so far

<!-- one line per closed ticket -->
- #230 (research): Workspace is already the Company (71/80 models keyed on workspaceId, one Bigcapital org per workspace, nothing above it); one login/many companies already works via per-workspace `WorkspaceMember.role`, the grouping is what is missing; both isolation layers key on `workspace_id`, so Companies should be an additive `Organization` + nullable `Workspace.organizationId` + `OrganizationMember`, with `WorkspaceMember` the only grant of entity access — [docs/research/multi-company-access.md](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/blob/research/multi-company-access/docs/research/multi-company-access.md); eight open decisions handed to #231.

- [Build the typed list-screen composition on all five queues (#225)](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/225) (task, shipped): the Queue screen is live on Invoices / POs / Receipts / Bank Statements / Exceptions — full-width 62px queue, one header band with facet chips, 60% right Detail pane with ↑/↓/Esc + sticky Approve/Reject, 56px icon rail, deep links; aging totals moved to the Dashboard as "Open invoices by age". In-page detector Invoices 30/26 · 41/34 → 6/5 · 6/5; critique 20/40 → 25/40. Critique findings with a decision became [#233](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/233) (one status vocabulary), [#234](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/234) (pane header stack), [#235](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/235) (below-md rendering — reopens a #224 choice, loop budget 1 of 2); the leading-glyph finding went to #223.

- [Shape the Approvals destination: Ready-to-Approve queues for Invoices and PO Mismatches (#227)](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/227) (grilling): a row is a *submitted* Approval at a stage, never a workflow-less ReviewTask; "me" = `canDecideStage`, surfaced as the personal system view Ready to Approve via #180's `scopeToCurrentUser`; PO Mismatches rows are blocked `match-variance` gates approved by `overrideGate(reason)`; ineligible rows (hard check, open Exception) stay visible and undecidable; same pane opening on Approval with read-only fields and a sticky Reject · Approve footer; Start from the Invoices bulk bar; decisions are Server-confirmed with no optimistic removal or Undo and no single-key approve; approval never publishes; incumbent critique 21/40, in-page 12/6 · 17/9. Execution: [#236](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/236). Glossary gained Approval, Approver, Ready to Approve, Send back for review, Not eligible.
- [Build the Approvals destination: Ready to Approve and PO Mismatches queues on the queue shell (#236)](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/236) (task, shipped `b137c01`): `/approvals/invoices` and `/approvals/po-mismatches` live on the #225 Queue-screen shell with deep links; `/review*` 308-redirects there; `review-inbox.tsx`/`review-task-detail.tsx` deleted. New `models/approvals.ts` (actor-scoped, deduped Ready-to-Approve count for the rail badge), `lib/approvals/row-eligibility.ts`, `startApprovalOnInvoice`/`sendReviewTaskBackForReview`/`cancelApprovalOnDocument`; `SplitPane` gained `initialTab`/`fieldsReadOnly` (locks fields while any stage is pending, in every Detail pane). All 16 of #227's decisions implemented as stated, including the full state-10 inventory and no optimistic removal/Undo. Verified: clean `tsc`, clean full-repo `eslint` on touched files, 2563/2563 tests (31 new), successful `next build` with all new routes in the manifest. **Gaps flagged:** `craft-floor.md` (referenced by this ticket and CLAUDE.md) doesn't exist anywhere in the repo's history; `impeccable`/`intent` still absent from the toolset (10th confirmation); mobile stays content-only pending #232; no live Postgres in this sandbox.
- [Decide what the operator app drops or folds to match the Vic grammar — starting with the Dashboard (#237)](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/237) (grilling): the workspace home is the Invoices queue on desktop and phone, no overview surface; the Dashboard's nine blocks are dropped (old page behind `DASHBOARD_LANDING` for one release), aging goes to #229 as Bill Pay's metric, KPIs and charts are removed and reporting is out of scope; rail loses Dashboard and the "Review" item, Controls/Close/Health/Activity wait for #231; Worksheets, Expenses and Dictation are **unplugged** at the owner's call (no nav, no actions, no badges, routes closed, code kept). - [Build the distilled operator shell: land on Invoices, drop the Dashboard, unplug Worksheets / Expenses / Dictation (#238)](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/238) (task, shipped `f99c8ac`): `/workspaces/<id>` lands on the Invoices queue; the old Dashboard survives one release at `/dashboard` behind `DASHBOARD_LANDING`; rail is Invoices · POs │ Receipts · Bank Statements │ Exceptions · Controls · Finance · Archive; phone tabs Invoices · Exceptions · Finance-or-Archive · Settings; Worksheets/Expenses/Dictation unplugged via `lib/unplugged` (four routes 404 in-shell, tested; code kept); a workspace not-found boundary keeps the rail on every dead address. Invoices landing in-page detector 7/5 → 7/5; incumbent Dashboard critique 20/40 archived; `evaluate` 74/100. H6 (11 rail stops) waits on #231; H7 and H10 graduated to [#240](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/240) (keyboard accelerators) and [#241](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/241) (first-run help after the Dashboard); the incumbent's 20/40 and its one good idea go to [#242](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/242).
